newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hambrecht takes stake in Israeli investment bank.
newsitem.headline: Hambrecht takes stake in Israeli investment bank.

text.p: Officials at Hambrecht and Quist said on Sunday they hoped that taking an equity stake in an Israeli investment bank would give them an edge over the other foreign investment banks in a crowded Israeli market.
"As other people opened offices we were trying to figure out what is that thing that jumps us ahead," Hambrecht's CEO and president Daniel Case told reporters in Tel Aviv.
The bank's top executives were in Israel to seal a deal in which they are investing $2 million in a newly formed Israeli investment bank, Tamir Fishman and Co, in exchange for a 33 percent holding.

Eldad Tamir, one Tamir Fishman's two partners, said it was the first time a U.S. investment bank is taking an equity position in an Israeli investment bank. Tamir and Danny Fishman control the other 67 percent.

"There are many excellent investment bankers and financial institutions in Israel but we thought this opportunity to back the best rising stars in finance who will be working together for many years was the right opportunity for us," Case said.
Hambrecht is a leading U.S. high technology-oriented investment bank, and Tamir Fishman will also have a technology focus.
Israeli companies, most of them in high technology, raised more than $1 billion in the United States last year.

"There is no question that American investors are interested in making investments in Israeli growth companies," said Hambrecht managing director Joshua Rafner, referring to the Jewish state as "a second Silicon Valley".
Tamir said political stability in the area, as a result of the Middle East peace process, contributed to Hambrecht's decision to take a stake in an Israeli investment bank.
